query: What pre-specified clinical-severity scoring rubric will we use, with concrete examples for minor/moderate/severe harm, and which patient outcomes/time windows will we link to errors?

response.query: What pre-specified clinical-severity scoring rubric will we use, with concrete examples for minor/moderate/severe harm, and which patient outcomes/time windows will we link to errors?
response.answer: We use the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) for clinical-severity scoring. Minor harm is grade 1, moderate is grade 2, and severe is grade 3-5. Outcomes linked to errors are adverse events within 30 days.

results.title: 421-Proctitis | eviQ
results.content: Radiation proctitis is a term used to describe radiation-induced injury to the rectal mucosa following radiation therapy to the pelvic area.r Depending on the time of onset, and to a lesser extent the clinical features and histology, radiation proctitis is defined as being either **acute** or **chronic**. Exact figures vary, but it is widely accepted that most patients receiving pelvic irradiation will develop some degree of acute radiation proctitis and approximately 1-5% of patients will experience chronic radiation proctitis.r However, it has been suggested that a much higher percentage of patients receiving pelvic radiation will have a permanent change to their bowel habits and for a significant number this may impair their quality of life.r The condition is probably underreported, as patients may be reluctant to report symptoms due to embarrassment or a belief that nothing can be done about them.rrr. There is also evidence that the occurrence and/or severity of acute radiation proctitis may be predictive of the development of chronic radiation proctitis.rrr This correlation may have implications for future preventative strategies and interventions.r.
